title: Your pencils
hint: HB, 2B and 6B (or any 3B-6B), plus a white eraser.
say: Three pencils today: an H-B for your lightest greys, a two-B for the mid-tones, and a six-B for your darkest darks -- any pencil from three-B to six-B works there. Any pencil works; sharpen it only when you need a fine detail. You'll also want a tissue for blending, and a white eraser -- or an eraser pencil, or a kneaded eraser pinched to a point -- for lifting highlights.

title: A tissue for blending
say: A small tissue blends your shading smooth once the tone is built up. We'll get there in a few steps -- for now, just know it's coming.

title: Feel your paper
hint: A little tooth helps the pencil grip.
say: Feel your own paper before you start. A little tooth helps the pencil grip -- that's what lets you build smooth, layered grey without the surface going shiny.

title: A steady centre line, then measure
watchSay: Before a single curve, the teacher marks the key heights straight down the centre line -- rim, neck, and base -- then transfers one measured width out to each side.
say: Mark your own centre line, step off the key heights down it, then transfer the same width to both sides with a small tick. Take your time.

card.title: A steady centre line, then measure
card.sub: Every key height marked, then the same width on both sides.

title: Square the round: straight lines find the bottle
watchSay: Notice there's no curve yet -- the rim, the neck, the shoulder and the body all start as short straight segments, tangent to where the round parts will be.
say: Try the same approach on your own bottle: block in the rim, neck, shoulder and body with short straight lines first. Go at your own pace.

card.title: Square the round: straight lines find the bottle
card.sub: Short straight segments, not one single curve.

title: Base down, then step back and check
watchSay: Hands come off the page for a moment -- one last look at the whole bottle, checking that both sides still match the centre line before moving on.
say: Hold your own drawing at arm's length and check both sides against your centre line. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: A steady shape, checked against itself
card.sub: Ready to place it on the page.

title: Structure complete
hint: Straight lines gave you a steady bottle — next, composition: where it sits on the page.
say: Straight lines gave you a steady bottle shape. That control now carries into every curve ahead. Next, we bring in composition — where it sits on the page.

title: Check the centre axis
watchSay: A single horizontal line crosses the shoulder here, with a small tick at each end -- checking that both sides still match the centre line, the same distance out.
say: Draw your own check-line across the widest point, with a tick on each side. Compare both distances from your centre line before moving on.

card.title: Check the centre axis
card.sub: The same distance out, on both sides.

title: Three tangent lines round the neck
watchSay: Like a cylinder, the neck curves inward in perspective -- never flat. Short tangent lines, not one arc: that's ‘square the round,’ and it's faster and more accurate than guessing a curve. One strategy among several, not the only way.
say: Add a couple of short tangent lines at your own neck, the same way. A few straight segments find the curve quicker than guessing an arc.

card.title: Three tangent lines round the neck
card.sub: Square the round — faster and more accurate than a guess.

title: The rim becomes an ellipse
watchSay: The rim's straight-sided box from before is now a full ellipse -- the first real curve in the whole drawing.
say: Round your own rim into an ellipse now, the same way. Take it slowly -- this curve sets the tone for the ones still to come.

card.title: The rim becomes an ellipse
card.sub: The first real curve in the whole drawing.

title: A quick correction, then keep going
watchSay: Even the teacher corrects a line here. In glass, small details carry real weight: the rim's thickness, a lip that sticks out just slightly, a highlight that will run down the body. Noticing these trains your eye.
say: Check your own rim for the same details -- its thickness, the small lip, where a highlight might run. Adjust anything that needs it, and take your time.

card.title: A quick correction, then keep going
card.sub: Rim thickness, the lip, a highlight still to come.

title: Tangents become curves
watchSay: The teacher stays right at the rim for a long stretch here -- the straight tangent lines from before slowly round into real curves as the shape gets found, not redrawn all at once.
say: Stay with your own rim a little longer too. Let each straight segment soften into a curve, bit by bit.

card.title: Tangents become curves
card.sub: Found slowly, not redrawn all at once.

title: Base down, left and right
watchSay: Same idea as the cylinder's base: dot the left and right edges first, before any curve. That's how the base's perspective -- and the glass's illusion -- gets found.
say: Mark your own base's left and right edges with a small dot each, the same way. The curve comes next, once those two points are set.

card.title: Base down, left and right
card.sub: Dot the edges first — the curve comes next.

title: A steady base, a shadow to ground it
watchSay: The base becomes a full ellipse here too, and a soft cast shadow grounds the bottle on the page.
say: Finish your own base as a full ellipse, then add a light shadow beneath it. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: A steady base, a shadow to ground it

title: Composition complete
hint: Every curve came from a straight line or a dotted point first — next, texture and light.
say: Every curve on this bottle came from a straight line or a dotted point first -- the centre axis, the neck, the rim, the base. Next, we bring in texture and light.
